items.title: Abe Most interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 13, 1999
items.q: So that was my entree to Fox Studios... it was Frank Beach, the first trumpet—

ctx.x: What was the military stint like for you?

It was one of the most gratifying, and I’m sorry to say nicest, supposed to be — in the military and I just had a ball because I learned how to write, how to arrange, and I learned how to play flute from one of the fellows in the band and it was great. There were great musicians from the west coast. That’s what enabled me to come out and go to Twentieth Century Fox. After the service, which was about three and a half years from ’42 to the © Fillius Jazz Archive -7-

middle of ’45, I went back. Nothing much was happening, we did a little something and then I came back here and pretty soon — oh I went back with Tommy in ’46 — not back with Tommy, back with Les. Tommy was first. In ’46 my wife Gussie and I decided to get married and we were on the road for a year with Tommy Dorsey and then that would have been ’47, and then a little kidding around, I think we went back to New York for a while, then I went back with Les from about ’48 to ’50.
